title: Lift Yourself
annotation: Teased for days as a serious statement in the middle of Kanye's chaotic spring 2018, the song turned out to be an Amnesty soul loop followed by roughly thirty seconds of improvised scat syllables about scooping poop. It is maybe the most famous troll in hip-hop history, and the closest thing this site has to a national anthem.
note: The entire vocal section is nonsense syllables built around scooping and pooping.

title: Think U the Shit (Fart)
annotation: A diss track whose entire premise is a fart joke in the title: the target thinks they're the best, but they're actually just gas. It charted on the Hot 100, which means a song with 'fart' in the parentheses was officially a hit.
note: Title and hook built on the you-think-you're-the-shit / you're-just-a-fart contrast.

title: Red Bull
annotation: Redman is the patron saint of gross-out rap, and his guest verse here is the canonical crowded-room fart joke.
note: Pun-heavy flatulence joke set in a crowded room.

title: Hidden Darts
annotation: A silent-but-deadly aside from one of the most vivid writers in rap, delivered with the same intensity he brings to everything else.
note: Tongue-in-cheek joke about a silent but smelly fart.

title: The Gas Face
annotation: An early entry in the canon. The title is the face you make when something stinks, and the song hands out gas faces to a long list of people who deserve one.

title: Toot It and Boot It
annotation: Not technically about flatulence, but the title is a toot joke whether YG meant it or not, and Complex ruled it eligible. We defer to Complex.

title: Ether
annotation: One of the most celebrated diss tracks ever made contains a fart joke. This is why the site exists.

title: Hot in Herre
annotation: A number-one single whose hook contains a smell joke that everyone sang along to without thinking about it.
note: Hook built around a smell-based joke.

title: The Vapors
annotation: Biz Markie built a career on being gross and lovable. 'The Vapors' is nominally about people who ignored you until you got famous, but Biz can't help himself.

title: E.T. (Extraterrestrial)
annotation: Big Boi drops a bathroom comparison into an otherwise menacing verse, which is the OutKast way: the weirdest possible image at the least expected moment.
note: Bathroom comparison inside a verse about violence.

title: Steady Mobbin'
annotation: In the middle of a day-in-the-life narrative, Cube stops to use the bathroom and reports on how much better he feels afterward. Peak early-90s storytelling: nothing is too small to narrate.
note: Describes stopping to use the bathroom and feeling relieved.

title: Restroom Occupied
annotation: The restroom here is occupied for reasons that have nothing to do with this site's subject matter, but the title alone earns it a spot in the Toilets category.

title: I Wanna Rock (Doo Doo Brown)
annotation: A Miami bass staple with 'Doo Doo' right there in the parenthetical. Miami New Times put it on their list of the top poop tunes of all time.

title: Funky Dividends
annotation: A Philly classic whose title, per Complex, is a joke about what happens after late-night eating.
note: Title tied to the aftermath of late-night eating.

title: A Milli
annotation: Lil Wayne is the undisputed king of this genre. Vice counted 99 separate poop references across his catalog, and 'A Milli', his signature mixtape-era-energy single, is one of them.

title: Mr. Carter
annotation: On a track with Jay-Z, Wayne sends his rivals down the drain. Flushing-as-dismissal is one of his favorite moves.

title: Dear Anne (Stan Part 2)
annotation: A sequel to Eminem's 'Stan' that pauses for a scene on the toilet. Wayne will put a bathroom in any song, including a sad one.

title: 500 Degreez
annotation: Early-career Wayne, already making stomachache jokes on a title track.

title: Money on My Mind
annotation: Wayne addresses a toilet directly. Few rappers have talked to more plumbing fixtures.

title: I'm Me
annotation: One of the great Wayne boast tracks includes an incontinence joke. Of course it does.

title: Bill Gates
annotation: A pun that connects talking with defecating. Rap has a long tradition of 'talking shit' wordplay; Wayne takes it literally.

title: Gonorrhea
album: I Am Not a Human Being
annotation: The title is a different bodily problem, but the poop reference is Wayne's: a classic 'shitting on rappers' boast.

title: Green and Yellow
annotation: A Packers anthem recorded for the 2011 Super Bowl that still finds room to insult someone for not having a bathroom.

title: Lollipop (Remix)
annotation: Kanye's remix verse on Wayne's biggest hit contains a skid-mark joke. Two of the most famous rappers alive, one of the biggest songs of 2008, and skid marks.

title: HYFR (Hell Ya Fucking Right)
annotation: Wayne's feature on one of Take Care's biggest singles includes a toilet-paper joke.

title: I'm Goin' In
annotation: Wayne's verse on the So Far Gone standout narrates a trip to the toilet.

title: Successful
annotation: An aspirational anthem about wanting the money, cars, and clothes, interrupted by a Wayne smell comparison.

title: Ignant Shit
annotation: Over the 'Ignorant Shit' beat, Wayne makes a toilet-paper-and-diarrhea joke. So Far Gone has three entries on this site, all of them Wayne's fault.

title: Miss Me
annotation: Wayne's verse, recorded shortly before his prison sentence, has a feces-related joke that is not for the faint of heart.

title: Roman's Revenge 2.0
annotation: The version of 'Roman's Revenge' where Wayne replaces Eminem, and brings a diaper joke with him.

title: Mercy (Remix)
annotation: Wayne boasts about being excrement. In his catalog this is a compliment.

title: Look at Me Now
annotation: Busta's verse is the famous one. Wayne's verse is the one with the pollution comparison that put it on this site.

title: Started From the Bottom
annotation: Complex counted it as a fart anthem on the strength of a 'bottom' pun. We're including it on a provisional basis, pending a ruling from the community.
